f.title: Include the risk management plan and its summary in a centralised marketing authorisation application
f.statement: Each centralised application shall specifically and completely include the particulars and documents referred to in Article 8(3) of Directive 2001/83/EC (among others), which include under point (iaa) the risk management plan describing the risk management system the applicant will introduce, together with its summary.
f.applicability: Applications for centralised marketing authorisation of medicinal products for human use

f.title: Implement the safe-use measures recommended in the CHMP opinion and imposed as conditions, within the risk management system
f.statement: A favourable CHMP opinion annexes details of any recommended measures for ensuring safe use of the medicinal product to be included in the risk management system. Where these become conditions of the marketing authorisation, the MAH must take the measures and incorporate them in its risk management system (Art 14a).
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Art 9(4)(ca); 14a; cf. Directive 2001/83/EC Art 21a(a)
f.applicability: Centralised marketing authorisations granted with conditions under Art 9(4)(ca)

f.title: Conduct the PASS or meet the stricter adverse reaction reporting obligations recommended by CHMP and imposed as conditions
f.statement: Where appropriate, a favourable CHMP opinion annexes details of any recommended obligation to conduct post-authorisation safety studies or to comply with recording or reporting obligations for suspected adverse reactions stricter than those in Chapter 3. Where these become conditions of the marketing authorisation, the MAH must comply and incorporate them in its risk management system (Art 14a).

f.applicability: Centralised marketing authorisations granted with conditions under Art 9(4)(cb)
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Conduct the PAES recommended by CHMP and imposed as an MA condition
f.statement: Where appropriate, a favourable CHMP opinion annexes details of any recommended obligation to conduct post-authorisation efficacy studies where concerns about aspects of efficacy are identified and can be resolved only after marketing, based on the delegated acts under Art 10b and taking into account the scientific guidance under Art 108a of Directive 2001/83/EC. Where this becomes a condition of the marketing authorisation, the MAH must conduct the studies and incorporate the condition in its risk management system (Art 14a).
f.applicability: Applications for centralised marketing authorisation of medicinal products for human use

f.title: Conduct a PASS imposed by the Agency after authorisation (a joint PASS is encouraged where concerns are shared)
f.statement: After authorisation the Agency may impose on the MAH an obligation to conduct a post-authorisation safety study if there are concerns about the risks of an authorised medicinal product; where imposed, the MAH must conduct it. If the same concerns apply to more than one product, the Agency shall, after consulting the PRAC, encourage the MAHs concerned to conduct a joint PASS.
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Art 10a(1)(a); cf. Directive 2001/83/EC Art 22a(1)(a)
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised under Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 (centralised procedure)
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.title: Conduct a PAES imposed by the Agency, to the objectives and timeframe in the notification
f.statement: After authorisation the Agency may impose on the MAH an obligation to conduct a post-authorisation efficacy study when the understanding of the disease or the clinical methodology indicates that previous efficacy evaluations might have to be revised significantly; the obligation is based on the delegated acts under Art 10b, taking into account the scientific guidance under Art 108a of Directive 2001/83/EC. The imposition is duly justified, notified in writing and includes the objectives and timeframe for submission and conduct of the study; where imposed, the MAH must conduct the study within that timeframe.

f.title: Request, within 30 days of the written notification, the opportunity to present written observations on an imposed study
f.statement: The MAH may, within 30 days of receipt of the written notification of an imposed PASS or PAES obligation, request an opportunity to present written observations, which it then submits within the time limit the Agency specifies.

f.title: Update the risk management system when the Commission confirms an imposed study obligation as an MA condition
f.statement: On the basis of the MAH’s written observations and the Agency’s opinion, the Commission withdraws or confirms the obligation; where the Commission confirms it, the marketing authorisation is varied to include it as a condition and the risk management system shall be updated accordingly.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised under Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 (centralised procedure)

f.title: Meet the safety, incident notification and action conditions of an MA granted in exceptional circumstances, reassessed annually
f.statement: In exceptional circumstances and after consulting the applicant, a marketing authorisation may be granted subject to conditions, in particular on the safety of the product, notification to the competent authorities of any incident relating to its use, and action to be taken; where imposed, the MAH must meet them. It may be granted only where the applicant shows, for objective and verifiable reasons, that it cannot provide comprehensive efficacy and safety data under normal conditions of use, on one of the grounds in Annex I to Directive 2001/83/EC. Continuation of the authorisation is linked to the annual reassessment of these conditions.
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Art 14(8); cf. Directive 2001/83/EC Art 22
f.applicability: Centralised marketing authorisations granted in exceptional circumstances
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Benefit–risk review; Submission operations

f.statement: As part of the specific obligations of a conditional marketing authorisation, which are specified, with any time limit for compliance, in the conditions to the authorisation and reviewed annually by the Agency, the holder shall complete ongoing studies or conduct new studies with a view to confirming that the risk-benefit balance is favourable.

f.title: Meet the Article 104 Directive duties, including operating an RMS per product and monitoring RMP outcomes, for centrally authorised products
f.statement: The MAH obligations in Article 104 of Directive 2001/83/EC apply to MAHs of centrally authorised products, including the duties to operate a risk management system for each medicinal product (104(3)(c)), to monitor the outcome of risk minimisation measures in the risk management plan or laid down as conditions (104(3)(d)), and to update the risk management system (104(3)(e)).
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised under Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 (centralised procedure)
f.exceptions: Holders of marketing authorisations granted before 2 July 2012 are not required to operate a risk management system for each product (Art 21(1) second subparagraph), unless the Agency imposes one under Art 21(2).
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.title: Inform the authorities before or with any public PV announcement and keep it objective, for centrally authorised products
f.statement: The MAH obligations in Article 106a(1) of Directive 2001/83/EC apply to safety announcements on centrally authorised products: the MAH shall inform the national competent authorities, the Agency and the Commission as soon as it intends a public announcement on pharmacovigilance concerns, and at the latest at the same time, and shall ensure the information is objective and not misleading.

f.statement: The Agency, the national competent authorities and the MAH shall inform each other when new risks, changed risks or changes to the risk-benefit balance are detected.

f.title: Follow the Directive PASS procedure (protocol, amendments, final report within 12 months, abstract) for imposed PASS of centralised products
f.statement: For non-interventional PASS of centrally authorised products that fulfil a requirement of Articles 10 or 10a, the procedure in Article 107m(3) to (7), Articles 107n to 107p and Article 107q(1) of Directive 2001/83/EC applies. The MAH must therefore not run promotional studies, limit HCP payments, monitor study data, submit the draft protocol for endorsement before starting, submit substantial amendments before implementation, submit the final study report within 12 months of the end of data collection with an abstract, and evaluate the impact on the authorisation.
f.applicability: Non-interventional PASS of centrally authorised products imposed under Art 10 or 10a
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies; Submission operations

Directive 2001/83/EC shall apply.

f.title: The Agency monitors selected medical literature for listed active substances and enters relevant information into EudraVigilance
f.statement: The Agency shall monitor selected medical literature for reports of suspected adverse reactions to medicinal products containing certain active substances, publish the list of active substances monitored and the medical literature subject to this monitoring, and enter relevant information from the selected literature into the EudraVigilance database. The MAH consequence (no reporting of ICSRs from the listed literature; monitor all other literature) is in Directive 2001/83/EC Art 107(3).
f.applicability: Medicinal products containing active substances on the EMA medical literature monitoring list
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up
